items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: the band that was playing down in the cellar was the great white father, Paul Whiteman.

ctx.x: Would Bojangles be appearing in a theater?

He'd be appearing somewhere in town, in a picture or theater or something. But we would always know that he was going to be there and we'd play for him right off the top of our heads. Whatever he wanted to play, we'd do those things. Mildred Bailey used to come by when she first came out with Paul Whiteman. She used to come by and sit and sing with us. All of the good stars, they came into that place because that was the top nightclub of the West and it was during

Prohibition time and that was one of the few places where you could go and find a first-class nightclub that went on until four and five o'clock in the morning. After everything was over in Hollywood at the Coconut Grove, they started heading toward the Apex. That's where it was. That was just a little bit before Bing Crosby went to work in the Coconut Grove with Gus Arnheim (PHONETIC). I was working at the Sebastian's Hide Cotton Club with Les Haight (PHONETIC) at the time that Bing Crosby was doing his --…

items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: The King of Jazz. He was working in the cellar and my old man was working in the main dining room.

ctx.x: But he was called to play with his orchestra for a course of time in the main dining room of the Santa Barbara Hotel for the dinners and such, and lo and behold, the band that was playing down in the cellar was the great white father, Paul Whiteman.
The King of Jazz. He was working in the cellar and my old man was working in the main dining room.
